resources.string: The apps you open or make are kept here. Start with an example below.
It\'s removed from Your apps, and its home-screen shortcut stops working.
Open source under the MIT licence, with no ads, no account and no data collected. The format reference, a guide for AI apps and more examples are on GitHub.
Change an example with Edit this app in its ⋮ menu, and your version is kept under Your apps.
A JSON file is plain text that describes an app: its screens, the words and pictures on them, lists, forms and buttons, and what happens when you tap something.
Open a file and it runs straight away as a real app on your phone. Nothing to install, build or sign up for.
Try an example below, open a file someone sent you, write one in the built-in editor, or ask the AI app you already use (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude…) to make one for you.
Every app you open is kept under Your apps. Put any of them on your phone\'s home screen with its own icon: tapping it opens that app directly.
Write one yourself: read the JSON format guide
Inside an app, its ⋮ menu lets you edit it, ask your AI app to change it, put it on your home screen, or come back here.
